round robin (rr) each process gets a small unit of cpu time (time quantum), usually 10-100 milliseconds. after this time has elapsed, the process is preempted and added to the end of the ready queue. if there are n processes in the ready queue and the time quantum is q, then each process gets 1/n of the cpu time in chunks of at most q time units at once. no process waits more than (n-1)q time units. performance z q large ⇒fifo z q small ⇒q must be large with respect to context switch, otherwise overhead is too high
